title: Guard battery sysfs rate against bogus EC readings
head: 05f1edc17570
workflow: Opus full review, Sol boundary hunter, Opus self-check of the draft, editorial check, batch gates

leads.summary: Charging time uses integer-rounded full energy rather than UPower's fractional energy-full
leads.consequence: When UPower omits time, a battery at 55.8 Wh of 56.7 Wh charging at 2 W should have ~27 minutes to full, but the script computes (56 - 55.8) / 2 and prints time 6m. The one-line notification says 6m to full; on the common case where UPower's rate itself is zero the power panel hides the time row entirely (H10), rather than correcting the calculation. Keep the full-precision energy-full separately from the rounded Wh display.

leads.summary: No fallback for batteries with energy_now but without charge_now, or charge_now without voltage_now
leads.consequence: UPower can read energy_now/energy_avg and energy_full on energy-unit batteries without any charge_now; charge-unit batteries can also use voltage_avg/design when voltage_now is absent. The new delta fallback silently declines these producer-supported shapes, leaving a wedged UPower rate at rate 0W and time blank in the open power panel indefinitely, even though energy deltas can be measured. Synthetic energy-only fixture at the pinned head prints rate 0W/time empty with 27.7 Wh available. Provide an energy_now delta path (and only infer from charge with available voltage source).
leads.triage: already N1 note (energy_now-only); voltage_avg subcase not published

leads.summary: Cache survives a non-sampleable state transition and can be reused on return to the same state or after a pack swap
leads.consequence: pending-charge, fully-charged or a temporary missing charge_now bypasses the entire cache write/clear. A discharging BAT0 sample from before an AC interruption is reused when BAT0 is discharging again within 600 s; a replacement pack on the same BAT0 native path likewise matches despite changed physical battery. This contradicts the code's claim that AC transitions and swapped packs can never borrow an old sample. In a synthetic discharging -> pending-charge -> discharging sequence with current zero UPower and bad sysfs, the last reading was 6.5W (from the pre-transition sample) rather than 0W/new-window. Require continuity across skipped states and, when available, battery serial/model identity or reset history on discontinuity.

leads.summary: Malformed cache charge/voltage fields are not validated before arithmetic
leads.consequence: The reader validates only the timestamp. A corrupted or tampered same-battery/state cache row supplies nonnumeric charge or voltage to shell arithmetic. Synthetic 'junk' cached charge makes the script quietly print rate 0W/time blank even though a subsequent good row could be used; a 'junk' cached voltage produces a false 3.2W and time 8h 44m instead of 6.5W and 4h 22m. The cache defaults to /tmp if XDG_RUNTIME_DIR is absent, so this is not necessarily trusted input. Validate all cached numeric fields (and reject malformed rows) before arithmetic.

leads.summary: Locale-formatted UPower energy is rejected by the new time fallback
leads.consequence: UPower's CLI enables the user's locale and formats energy with %g. In decimal-comma locales it can print energy: 28,3 Wh; the new strict dot-decimal test fails and the omitted remaining-time field stays empty, so the panel shows an em dash even with a usable rate. Synthetic UPower-format comma fixture outputs time empty. Parse UPower's locale with a matching numeric conversion or explicitly invoke upower under LC_ALL=C and parse consistently; existing rate/capacity parsing also has locale pitfalls, but this is the new time-derivation path.
leads.triage: dropped: decimal comma falls back to base behaviour (no time); pre-existing locale issues

leads.summary: Related #13111 has an incompatible sysfs-rate policy and conflicting fixture
leads.consequence: #13111's pinned diff explicitly accepts a 60W sysfs reading when UPower reports 8W and tests for rate 60W, whereas #13009's 3x guard rejects it and prints 8W. Both branches modify the same guard and test file; combining them without choosing a policy will either fail that test or violate this PR's bound. git merge-file with the other PR's merge base produces conflict markers in the rate guard and the test (not a clean merge), even though GitHub reports #13111 MERGEABLE against its own base. Coordinate the intended threshold and tests if both merge.
leads.triage: verified by coordinator read of #13111 diff/test and by Opus draft check; published as note

leads.summary: The new time fallback treats pending-charge as discharging if UPower omits its time
leads.consequence: A pending-charge battery with UPower rate 0W/no time and a separately accepted sysfs 2W receives energy/rate as a 'time to empty'; the CLI notification says '27h 53m left' for a pending-charge battery if no charge threshold is available, even if the machine is on AC. When an AC threshold exists the separate holding-label branch hides this time from the notification. UPower can emit pending-charge and omit time when rate is zero; a live sysfs rate can still pass the guard. Synthetic pending-charge/no-time fixture with 55.8Wh UPower energy/0W UPower rate and 2W sysfs prints 27h 53m. Only derive empty for discharging and full for charging.
leads.triage: dropped: requires UPower 0 W with accepted non-zero sysfs in pending-charge; else branch mirrors UPower 1.91.3 (Opus); panel hides time in holding states

leads.summary: Power panel suppresses the new charging-time fallback precisely when UPower reports 0W
leads.consequence: On a single charging battery whose UPower EnergyRate is wedged at 0W, the script can infer a nonempty time from an accepted sysfs rate or charge-delta estimate and print a time row. The panel independently reads Quickshell's UPower.displayDevice.changeRate, which is bound to the same D-Bus EnergyRate; at 0 W, Model.chargeThresholdActive returns true even without a charge threshold, so Panel.qml labels the row 'Charge limit' and displays a threshold or '-' instead of batteryInfo.time, and labels the battery Holding. A synthetic Model.js run with rate 0/time 4h 22m shows the suppression; no rendered panel was tested. Expose the estimated rate/state to the panel or condition the threshold heuristic on real threshold metadata before asserting that derived time restores the panel row.
leads.triage: behavioural; Opus follow-up (opus/followup-1.md) confirmed from source, base behaviour; published as note

leads.summary: Changed fixtures only exercise discharging time and do not catch truncating charging energy-full
leads.consequence: The new wedge and no-time fixtures set state discharging, so an implementation that rounds full battery energy before charging-time arithmetic passes every added time assertion, as the pinned head actually does. Add a charging/no-time fixture with UPower rate 0W, accepted sysfs rate 2W, energy-full 56.7 Wh, energy 55.8 Wh, then assert time 27m, which would fail on the current 6m output. A discharging -> pending-charge -> discharging sequence would likewise detect the separate cache continuity issue H3; the existing 'other state' test starts with only a charging cache row and does not exercise returning to a previously cached state.
leads.triage: folded into N-C ('no tests cover the charging branch') and N-A optional test note

leads.summary: #13292's real-battery selection and per-pack sysfs guards conflict with this PR's new early cache path
leads.consequence: The separate open PR #13292 selects a BAT1 with real energy-full instead of the phantom BAT0, and guards native-path resolution. Here BAT0 is still selected unconditionally and used to create a cache even when it is a phantom; merging both as-is has two unresolved hunks (the battery selection/guard and pack-specific fallbacks). Its fixture asserts BAT1's percentage/cycles/threshold; this PR's code retains BAT0. Manual integration must make the selected pack the identity for cache and all sysfs reads. This is a cross-PR integration lead, not a regression claimed unique to this PR.
leads.triage: dropped: #13292 integration context, not a regression of this PR

Charge-voltage fallback and locale are confirmed from UPower 1.91.3 source plus shaped input, not on hardware. Other open PRs touching the script and QML were inventoried but only overlapping #13111 and #13292 were pursued to issue-level merged outcomes.

comment:
## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

Follow-up to the [earlier automated review](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/13009#issuecomment-5822688300) of `ed23094` and the author's replies ([1](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/13009#issuecomment-5833649892), [2](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/13009#issuecomment-5843121643)). Checked revision: `05f1edc` ("Derive remaining time from energy when UPower omits it").

**Outcome:** Three of the earlier findings are resolved at `05f1edc`. The battery-identity finding is resolved for three of its four cases; the same-slot pack swap remains. The new 10-minute history introduces two new findings: after a suspend, a hold on AC or a same-slot pack swap, the estimate can stay badly wrong for several minutes (and the new remaining time with it), and cached charge and voltage fields reach shell arithmetic without validation. A smaller issue affects time to full.

### Earlier findings

| Earlier finding | Status at `05f1edc` | Synthetic result (12 V, 1 mAh steps, UPower at 0 W) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Estimate window restarts on every call | Resolved | Sysfs rejected, 5 s polling: 7.5 W load reads `7.3W`–`7.7W` after the first minute, instead of `8.6W`/`0W`. `0W` for the first 30 s, as the code comment describes. |
| Fallback replaces an accepted sysfs reading | Resolved | Accepted sysfs 0.9 A with a 60 s cache: `10.8W` (sysfs), previously `6.5W` (estimate) |
| Cached sample has no battery or state identity | Three of four cases resolved | Foreign battery, charging then unplugged, discharging then plugged in: now `0W` instead of a borrowed value. Same-slot pack swap: still wrong, see the first new finding. |
| Clock-dependent wedge test (optional) | Resolved | A `date` stub fixes the clock; the test passed 50 of 50 sandboxed runs |

**Verified:**
- The estimate now uses the oldest kept sample that is at least 30 s old, up to 600 s. It runs only when sysfs was absent or rejected, and each cache line records `native_path` and `state`.
- The author's UPower 1.91.3 matches the premise. Once a rate above 0.01 W has been seen, UPower keeps trusting the reported current and zeroes rates above 300 W. It computes a time only when its rate is above 0.01 W, and `upower -i` prints the time only when it is above 0. So a wedged 0 W rate also drops the time line, as the second reply describes.
- The new tests for sysfs preference and for foreign battery and state each fail when that guard is removed.

**Not rechecked:** The replies' statement that the full `./test/shell` failures match the base branch. Within `./test/shell`, only `battery-status-test.sh` runs this script.

### New: The 10-minute window spans suspend, AC holds and same-slot swaps

The window uses wall-clock timestamps (`date +%s`) and always measures from the oldest kept sample, up to 600 s old. Nothing resets the history when the reading is interrupted:
- The wall clock keeps running during suspend.
- `pending-charge`, `fully-charged` and `unknown` skip sampling but leave the cache as it is (`bin/omarchy-battery-status:109-116`), so a battery held at a charge limit on AC and then unplugged reuses samples from before the hold.
- A pack swapped into the same slot keeps `BAT0` and the same state, so it passes the identity check.

A window that includes little or no drain underestimates the rate, and the new time derivation divides energy by that rate, so the remaining time is inflated by the same factor. A swapped pack instead gives a rate that is far too high.

Synthetic timelines (10 W actual load, 0.5 W while suspended, 5 s polling while the panel is open; "settles" means first within 15% of the actual rate):

| Scenario | First estimate at `05f1edc` | Settles after | `ed23094` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Discharging with the panel open, suspended 180 s, panel reopened | `1.5W`, `31h 41m` left (about `4h 41m` once settled) | ~415 s | `1.1W` for one refresh, then `8.6W`/`17.3W` |
| Suspended 300 s with the panel open | `5.3W`, `8h 50m`, flat for ~5 min | ~305 s | `0.7W` for one refresh |
| Discharging 60 s, held on AC (`pending-charge`) 180 s, unplugged | `2.6W`, `18h 4m` | ~420 s | `0W` for one refresh, then `8.6W` |
| Same-slot pack swap, 30 W actual charge (script output; see the panel note below) | `0W` for ~20 s, then `147.7W`; about `50W` after 9 minutes | ~585 s | `36W` for one refresh |

UPower's own estimator discards its history on resume and on AC changes. The code comment at `:101-102` says "a swapped pack or an AC transition can never borrow a reading from the previous battery state"; the swap and AC-hold sequences above do. The earlier review suggested using the oldest sample within 600 s, and that suggestion did not account for these interruptions.

**Impact:** On the hardware this PR targets (where the UPower wedge persists across resume), opening the lid after a suspend, or unplugging after a hold at a charge limit, can show a rate several times too low with a remaining time several times too long, for several minutes. At `ed23094`, the carried-over sample affected only one refresh in these sequences. A steady load after a 5 W to 25 W step also takes about 8 minutes to reach within 15%.

**Suggested change:** A shorter maximum window, for example `maximum_window=120`, fixed all four scenarios in the synthetic runs. The first three recovered within about 30 s (`0W`, then about 10 W), the swap in about 2 minutes. A steady 7.5 W still read `7.2W`–`7.7W`, and the 5 W to 25 W step settled in 95 s instead of 485 s. The cost is `0W` for the first 30 s after any gap longer than 120 s. Alternatively, clearing the history when the gap between samples exceeds about 30 s and on any state other than charging or discharging fixed suspend, the AC hold and the swap in the synthetic runs, but not the slow response to a load step.

**Optional test improvement:** No test checks which sample is used as the reference. A variant that uses the youngest sample at least 30 s old passes the current test file.

### New: Cached charge and voltage fields are not validated before arithmetic

The cache reader checks only the timestamp (`:125`). The charge and voltage fields go straight into `$((charge_sample - sample_charge))` and `$(((volt_sample + sample_volt) / 2))` (`:139`, `:142`). `ed23094` checked all three fields against `^[0-9]+$`.

| Cache field (synthetic, estimate path) | `05f1edc` | `ed23094` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Charge containing a command substitution inside an array subscript | The command ran, and the line was kept in the rewritten cache | Line ignored |
| Charge `46abc` | `value too great for base` on stderr, rate `0W` | Line ignored |
| Voltage missing | `3.2W`, `8h 44m` (instead of `6.5W`, `4h 22m`) | Line ignored |

**Impact:** The cache normally sits in the user's own `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR`. When `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` is unset, it falls back to the fixed `/tmp/omarchy-battery-rate.cache`, which another local account could create first. The unchecked arithmetic only runs when the estimate runs, so the likelihood is low on a single-user laptop. A corrupt line still gives a wrong reading. Cross-account `/tmp` behavior was not tested.

**Suggested change:** Add `[[ $sample_charge =~ ^[0-9]+$ && $sample_volt =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || continue` to the read loop. Optionally, skip caching when `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` is unset.

### New: Time to full uses the truncated capacity

The charging branch computes `capacity - energy_now` (`:176-177`), but `capacity` is energy-full truncated to whole Wh for display (`:42`). Synthetic: 55.9 of 56.7 Wh charging at 5 W shows `1m`, while UPower's formula gives about 9.6 minutes. The error is at most 1 Wh divided by the rate, so it matters most near full.

**Impact:** Near full charge, the time to full is too short. It appears in the `omarchy-notification-battery` line, and in the panel from 99% up (see the note below).

**Suggested change:** Parse energy-full separately, without `%d`, for this calculation. None of the new tests cover the charging branch.

**Note (panel, base behavior):** While charging below 99% with UPower's rate at 0 W, the power panel does not show the script's estimated rate or derived time to full. `Model.chargeThresholdActive` treats a charging battery at 0.2 W or less as held (`shell/plugins/panels/power/Model.js:63`), so the panel shows "Charge limit" and "Holding" instead. This is unchanged from the base branch (source inspection, no rendered panel). Discharging, the case in the replies, is shown normally. The charging-side estimate currently reaches the user mainly through the notification.

**Note:** Open PR #13111 addresses the same bogus-current symptom with a different policy. It accepts a plausible sysfs rate far above UPower's (60 W against 8 W in its test), where this PR's 3x guard keeps UPower's 8 W. Both add a guard in the same sysfs-rate block and change the same test file.

**Note (unchanged):** When `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` is unset, the cache still falls back to the shared `/tmp`. Batteries that expose only `energy_now` still get no estimate.

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** Source inspection of `05f1edc` against `ed23094` and the base, UPower 1.91.3 and the power panel source, plus sandboxed runs of the head `battery-status-test.sh` and synthetic timelines with stubbed UPower and `date`, synthetic sysfs and a controlled clock. No real battery, EC, UPower daemon, suspend or rendered panel was used, and the full test suite was not run. The window figures are arithmetic predictions for the stated synthetic loads. Real firmware step sizes and suspend drain are unknown.

**AI process:** Opus 5.5 Medium coordination and synthesis, Opus 5.5 Xhigh technical review and final fact check, GPT 6 Sol Xhigh search for related issues, Opus 5.5 Medium editorial check.

**Opt out:** To stop receiving these reviews, reply to this comment saying so.
